2607.23319.title: BHARATI: Morphology-Aware Tokenizers for Classical Indian Languages with Subword Fertility Analysis
2607.23319.paper_summary: Standard subword tokenization algorithms such as Byte-Pair Encoding (BPE) and SentencePiece are trained predominantly on modern language corpora and produce inefficient segmentations when applied to classical Indian languages. Sanskrit, Tamil, and other classical Indic languages exhibit agglutinative morphology, productive sandhi (phonological fusion at word boundaries), and domain-specific vocabularies absent from general-purpose training data. This paper presents BHARATI, a set of SentencePiece BPE tokenizers trained on a balanced 781 MB corpus spanning seven languages (English, Hindi, Sanskrit, Tamil, Telugu, Kannada, and Malayalam) with native script support for all languages. We describe three successive tokenizer versions: v1 (English and Sanskrit only, with broken byte-fallback for Tamil), v2 (four-language support with byte-level fallback for southern languages), and v3 (full seven-language native subword coverage). Subword fertility analysis demonstrates that v3 averages 2.6 tokens per Indian Knowledge System (IKS) technical term, compared to 5.25 tokens per term with GPT-2's tokenizer and 3.75 tokens with the multilingual SentencePiece baseline, with the largest gains on a set of reserved IKS terms that are represented as single tokens by construction. On a held-out test set of 490 IKS-domain sentences (70 per language across seven languages, released with the measurement script), v3 reduces sequence length by roughly 90% relative to GPT-2 and byte-level encoding (which lack native Indic subwords) and by approximately 25% relative to the mBART-50 multilingual baseline, averaged across the six Indic languages, directly translating to increased effective context length for downstream language models. The tokenizer models (32,000 vocabulary), training scripts, and evaluation benchmarks are released under open licenses.
2607.23319.paper_summary_zh: 標準的子詞標記算法，如字節對編碼（BPE）和SentencePiece，主要在現代語言語料庫上進行訓練，並在應用於古典印度語言時產生低效的分段。梵語、泰米爾語和其他古典印度語言展現出粘合形態、豐富的音變（在單詞邊界的語音融合）以及缺乏於通用訓練數據的特定領域詞彙。本文提出了BHARATI，一組基於SentencePiece BPE的標記器，訓練於一個平衡的781 MB語料庫，涵蓋七種語言（英語、印地語、梵語、泰米爾語、泰盧固語、卡納達語和馬拉雅拉姆語），並支持所有語言的本地腳本。我們描述了三個連續的標記器版本：v1（僅支持英語和梵語，對泰米爾語有斷裂的字節回退）、v2（支持四種語言，對南方語言有字節級回退）和v3（完整的七種語言本地子詞覆蓋）。子詞豐富性分析顯示，v3平均每個印度知識系統（IKS）技術術語有2.6個標記，相比之下，GPT-2的標記器每個術語有5.25個標記，multilingual SentencePiece基準則為3.75個標記，對於一組由構造表示為單個標記的保留IKS術語，增益最大。在490個IKS領域句子的保留測試集上（每種語言70個，跨七種語言，隨測量腳本發布），v3相對於GPT-2和字節級編碼（缺乏本地印度子詞）將序列長度減少了約90%，相對於mBART-50多語言基準則減少了約25%，這是在六種印度語言中平均計算的，直接轉化為下游語言模型的有效上下文長度增加。標記器模型（32,000詞彙）、訓練腳本和評估基準在開放許可下發布。
